result:
I'd make curiosity and a commitment to understanding reality the default human setting.

Not blind optimism or enforced agreement—just a widespread, stubborn drive to figure out how things actually work, update when the evidence changes, and treat "I don't know yet" as a prompt rather than a threat. Most of the durable problems we face (needless conflict, stalled progress on energy and health, fragile institutions, self-inflicted scarcity) are downstream of motivated reasoning, tribal epistemology, and the refusal to look carefully at trade-offs. A species that systematically prefers accurate models of the world over comforting ones would still disagree, still compete, and still make mistakes—but it would compound knowledge instead of compounding error, and it would be far harder to manipulate.

Everything else—technology, institutions, resources—gets dramatically more tractable once that shift is in place.
